ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Ana plays with $n \times n$ boards by placing a token in each of the cells with no common points with other cells containing tokens. In the picture beside we see how to place as many chips as possible on $5 \times 5$ and $6 \times 6$ boards. In this way, how many chips can Ana possibly put on a $2020 \times 2020$ board?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the 5×5 chessboard on the left, the red pieces are placed at the intersections of rows 1, 3, 5 and columns 1, 3, 5, forming a total of 3×3=9 pieces; on the 6×6 chessboard on the right, the red pieces are also placed with one row and one column skipped, for a total of 3×3=9 pieces. The rule reflected in the figure is: any two squares with pieces cannot have a common point, that is, they cannot share an edge, nor can they touch only at a corner. Reasoning: For a 2020×2020 chessboard, it can be divided into non-overlapping 2×2 small squares. Any two cells in each 2×2 small square have a common edge or common vertex, so each 2×2 small square can contain at most 1 piece. Since 2020/2=1010, there are 1010×1010 such 2×2 small squares in total, so at most 1010^2 pieces can be placed. This upper bound can be achieved: place one piece in the same relative position in each 2×2 small square, and adjacent pieces will all be separated by one row or one column, with no common point.

method.method_draft: Read the picture first: the 5×5 board has tokens placed in every other row and every other column, giving a 3×3 pattern of 9 tokens; the 6×6 board similarly shows tokens separated by one empty row and one empty column, giving a 3×3 pattern. From the text, interpret “cells with no common points” as meaning no two chosen cells may share an edge or even a corner. Use the standard packing rule: in each pair of consecutive rows, at most one row can contain chosen cells adjacent vertically/diagonally to the next, and within a chosen row tokens must be in alternating columns, so the maximum is ceil(n/2)·ceil(n/2). For n=2020, this is 1010·1010 = 1010^2.

图像描述：左边的 5×5 棋盘上，红色棋子放在第 1、3、5 行和第 1、3、5 列的交点处，共形成 3×3=9 个棋子；右边的 6×6 棋盘上，红色棋子也隔一行、隔一列放置，共 3×3=9 个棋子。图中体现的规则是：任意两个放棋子的格子不能有公共点，也就是不能共边，也不能只在角上相接。

推理：对于 2020×2020 棋盘，可以把它分成互不重叠的 2×2 小方块。每个 2×2 小方块中的任意两个格子都有公共边或公共顶点，因此每个 2×2 小方块最多只能放 1 个棋子。因为 2020/2=1010，所以共有 1010×1010 个这样的 2×2 小方块，故最多放 1010^2 个棋子。这个上界可以达到：在每个 2×2 小方块的同一相对位置放一个棋子，相邻棋子之间都会隔开一行或一列，不会有公共点。
